week_thesis: AMD delivered a strong week after last Monday's entries, crossing the $1 trillion market cap milestone on September 22 — only the fourth US chipmaker to do so (+189% YTD, +12.7% from our $559 entry). At $630.63 AMD now trades 1–2% above the analyst mean consensus target ($616–$624), but the Q3 guide ($13B, +41% YoY), a 10% chip price hike, and strong AI accelerator demand support the bull case ($1,250 high-end target). NVDA holds at $225.07 with 45% upside to the $327 analyst median target and Q3 FY2027 guidance of ~$100B. Critical macro events this week: (1) MU earnings Wednesday Sep 30 after close — expected $51B revenue +353% YoY / EPS $31 vs $3 last year; consensus is bullish but 'guidance language is king' — any HBM pricing softness triggers sell-the-news; (2) September NFP Jobs Report Friday Oct 2 — the June 5 analog risk (-10.3% portfolio in one day). Action: hold AMD and NVDA through these events (AMD is GPU/accelerator not memory — limited fundamental correlation to MU), close de minimis MAN (housekeeping), no new buys given MU/NFP concentration risk this week. Post-NFP clarity (Oct 6+): MU re-entry if strong guidance, AVGO if post-earnings reset confirms AI setup.
